title: Quantifying the Persona Effect in LLM Simulations
measurement_description: The paper measured how an LLM's toxicity rating of a text is affected by a persona's self-reported importance of religion. It also evaluated the ability of LLMs to predict a persona's prayer frequency based on other demographic and social variables.
findings: As one of several persona variables, the self-reported importance of religion was found to have a small but measurable influence (ΔR² = 0.0128) on toxicity annotations. The frequency of prayer was found to be moderately predictable from other persona variables (Target R² = 0.40). The paper's general finding is that LLM simulations using persona variables (including religion) are more effective when those variables have a stronger correlation with the target human behavior.
